title: OpenAI lists new gpt-rosalind-discovery model in docs
key_facts: OpenAI's API pricing page appears to have been updated with a model the company has not announced, gpt-rosalind-discovery, under a 'Life sciences models' section beside gpt-rosalind-research.
The listing was first shared by the AI Tracker Bot on X; there is no blog post, help article or system card yet.
Both models cost the same: $5 per million input tokens, $0.50 per million cached input tokens and $25 per million output tokens.
Access to the Rosalind models is restricted through OpenAI's trusted-access program; billing for gpt-rosalind-research began on 5 Oct 2026.

GPT-Rosalind was introduced in April as a frontier reasoning model for biology, drug discovery and translational medicine, with partners including Amgen, Moderna, the Allen Institute and Thermo Fisher Scientific.
TestingCatalog says the name suggests a drug discovery model, but calls that a guess; OpenAI's exact purpose for the model is unclear.
quote_evidence: There's still no blog post, help article, or system card for it yet.
While the company hasn't exactly said what gpt-rosalind-discovery is, the name suggests it could be a drug discovery model.
For now, though, that's a guess.
why_it_matters_hint: A second Rosalind model on OpenAI's price list hints at a family of specialist life-science models, but nothing is confirmed.
notes: Read TestingCatalog in full. Single outlet, relying on a post by a tracker bot on X; the pricing page itself was not checked by us. Purpose of the model is TestingCatalog's guess.
